cards.title: Maintenance Loan

cards.description: Living-cost support paid to you if eligible.

cards.title: Tuition Fee Loan
cards.subTitle: £9k+
cards.description: Course-fee support usually paid to provider.

cards.title: Grants & bursaries
cards.subTitle: Check

section_3.title: Your student finance estimate.
section_3.description: This is an indicative result. Final entitlement depends on SFE assessment, course intensity, household income, location and study mode.

steppers.title: Confirm your status
steppers.description: SFE first checks who you are: your residency, nationality and whether you've studied before. This decides what you can get.

facts.title: Who qualifies
facts.description: Usually 3 years' UK residence + settled/eligible status

facts.title: Watch-out
facts.description: Previous study (ELQ) can reduce or block funding

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Have your passport/ID, residency history and any previous-study details ready before you start.

steppers.title: Your course must be designated
steppers.description: The loan only flows if your course and provider are SFE-designated. Distance-only and some part-time intensities are treated differently.

facts.title: Eligible
facts.description: Designated undergraduate courses at registered providers

facts.title: Not eligible
facts.description: Non-designated providers, most distance-only courses

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Confirm with the university that your specific course is SFE-designated for your start year.

steppers.title: SFE links to your provider
steppers.description: Once your course is confirmed, SFE connects your application to the university so they can verify your enrolment later.

facts.title: What SFE needs
facts.description: Provider name, course title and start date

facts.title: Timing
facts.description: Set up as soon as you have a firm offer

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Enter the exact provider and course as they appear on your offer letter.

steppers.title: Submit your application
steppers.description: You apply online through your regional Student Finance service. The Tuition Fee Loan is paid straight to the university — you never touch it.

facts.title: When to apply
facts.description: Open ~6 months before term; apply early

facts.title: Paid to
facts.description: Your university, directly, in instalments

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Apply even before you have a confirmed place — you can update details later.

steppers.title: Send your evidence
steppers.description: SFE may ask for identity, residency or household-income evidence. Missing documents are the most common cause of delay.

facts.title: Common asks
facts.description: Passport, residency proof, household income

facts.title: Risk
facts.description: Slow evidence = delayed first payment

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Upload everything SFE requests in one go, and keep copies.

steppers.title: SFE approves your funding
steppers.description: SFE assesses everything and confirms your entitlement. You'll get an entitlement letter showing your Tuition Fee Loan amount.

facts.title: Outcome
facts.description: Entitlement letter confirming amounts

facts.title: If wrong
facts.description: You can request a reassessment

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Check the entitlement letter carefully and query anything that looks off.

steppers.title: The loan is paid out
steppers.description: After you enrol and the university confirms attendance, SFE releases the tuition payment directly to the provider, in instalments across the year.

facts.title: Trigger
facts.description: University confirms your enrolment

facts.title: Schedule
facts.description: Usually three instalments per year

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: Make sure you fully enrol — payment won't release until the provider confirms.

steppers.title: You repay only when earning
steppers.description: Repayment is income-based and only starts above the Plan 5 threshold. Anything still owed after the term is written off — it's nothing like a commercial loan.

facts.title: You repay
facts.description: 9% of income above the threshold

facts.title: Write-off
facts.description: Remaining balance cleared after the set period

facts.title: Do this:
facts.description: You don't repay a penny while earning under the threshold — keep your contact details current with SLC.

section_8.title: Who usually needs a funding check?
section_8.description: A quick student-first view before they start an application.

cards.title: British / Irish
cards.subTitle: Usually strong route
cards.description: Typically checked for England residence, course designation and previous study.

cards.title: Settled / ILR
cards.subTitle: Full support route
cards.description: Often eligible for tuition and maintenance support if residence rules are met.

cards.title: Pre-settled
cards.subTitle: Needs review
cards.description: Can be possible, but residence history and category matter. Do not guess.

cards.title: Refugee / protection
cards.subTitle: Protected route
cards.description: Often eligible for strong support, but documents and dates must be checked.

section_9.title: From eligibility to repayment.
section_9.description: Students understand finance faster when the process is shown as a journey, not a wall of rules.

cards.title: 1. Eligibility
cards.description: Check nationality, immigration status, ordinary residence, age and previous study.

cards.title: 2. Application
cards.description: Submit SFE details, evidence and course information early to avoid delayed payments.

cards.title: 3. Payments
cards.description: Tuition goes to the provider. Maintenance is paid to the student after enrolment confirmation.

cards.title: 4. Repayment
cards.description: Repay only when earning above the threshold. It is income-based, not a normal bank loan.

section_10.title: Finance explained without panic.
section_10.description: These blocks should reduce fear and increase adviser enquiries.

rows.myth: “Student Finance is like a bank loan.”
rows.reality: Repayment is based on income, not a fixed monthly instalment.
No. Repayment starts only after the course and only above the income threshold.

rows.myth: “If I studied before, I cannot get anything.”
rows.reality: Previous study matters, but rules vary by route and qualification.

rows.myth: “Online and weekend courses are always the same.”
rows.reality: Mode and attendance can affect maintenance support.
